title: Configuring SAML for Microsoft Azure Active Directory Single Sign-On

blocks.text: Zscaler recommends using Authentication Service to configure primary and secondary external identity providers (IdPs). Authentication Service supports both SAML and OpenID configurations. Contact Zscaler Support to subscribe to Authentication Service.
This article provides information on how to configure Microsoft Azure Active Directory (AD) as a SAML identity provider (IdP) for single sign-on (SSO).
Make sure that the following prerequisites are met:

blocks.item: You have access to the Azure AD service with a privileged user role, preferably the Global Administrator role.
Browsers can access the following URLs:
*.azure.com
*.illusionblack.com
Remove any proxy restrictions on these URLs.

blocks.heading: Configuring SAML for Azure AD Single Sign-On

blocks.text: To configure Azure AD as a SAML IdP for SSO:

blocks.item: Step 1: Configure an Enterprise Application in Azure AD for SSO
Log in to the Azure portal with the Global Administrator role.
Go to Azure Active Directory > Enterprise applications.
The All applications page opens.
Click New application.
See image.
The Browse Azure AD Gallery page opens.
Click Create your own application
See image.
In the Create your own application window:
Enter a name for your application.
Select Integrate any other application you don't find in the gallery (Non-gallery).
See image.
Don't click any of the recommended applications that might match your application name.
Click Create.
The enterprise application is created.
See image.
Step 2: Obtain the Azure AD SAML Metadata
Open the enterprise application that you created.
In the left-side navigation, select Single sign-on.
See image.
On the Single sign-on page, click SAML.
See image.
On the SAML-based Sign-on page, under SAML Certificates, copy the URL in App Federation Metadata Url and paste it into your browser to download the metadata XML file.
See image.
Step 3: Create a SAML Provider for Azure AD in the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal
Configure SAML for SSO in the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal. In the SAML Provider Details window, make sure you unselect Encryption and Sign Get Request, and select Use Dedicated Certificate.
Upload the metadata XML file that you downloaded.
Obtain the SAML XML file from the Deception Admin Portal. To learn more, see Obtaining SAML Setup Information.
Step 4: Configure SSO for the Enterprise Application
Log in to the Azure portal with the Global Administrator role.
Open the enterprise application that you created.
In the left-side navigation, select Single sign-on.
On the Set up Single Sign-On with SAML page, click Upload metadata file.
See image.
In the Upload metadata file window, browse and select the metadata XML file that you downloaded, and then click Add.
See image.
In the Basic SAML Configuration window, click Save.
See image.
On the SAML-based Sign-on page, under SAML Certificates, click Download for Federation Metadata XML.
See image.
The federation metadata XML file is downloaded.
Log in to the Deception Admin Portal.
Go to Settings > Users & Roles > IdP Providers.
Click the Edit icon for the SAML SSO entry that you created for Azure AD.
In the SAML Provider Details window, click Upload to upload the federation metadata XML that was downloaded.
Click Save.
See image.
Step 5: Add a User or Group Account to the Enterprise Application
Log in to the Azure portal with the Global Administrator role.
Open the enterprise application that you created.
In the left-side navigation, select Users and groups, and then select Add user/group.
See image.
In the Add Assignment window:
Under Users, click None Selected.
The Users window opens.
Search for the user you want to assign to the enterprise application.
Click Select.
See image.
Click Assign.
See image.
The User Principal Name of the user in the Azure portal must match the Email field of the user created in the Deception Admin Portal.
After configuring the SSO, log out of the Deception Admin Portal, and sign in with Azure AD SSO.
See image.
(Optional) Step 6: Configure SAML Group Provisioning for Azure
Log in to the Azure portal with the Global Administrator role.
Open the enterprise application that you created.
In the left-side navigation, select Single sign-on.
On the Set up Single Sign-On with SAML page, under Attributes & Claims, click Edit.
See image.
On the Attributes & Claims page, click Add a group claim.
See image.
In the Group Claims window:
For Which groups associated with the user should be returned in the claim?, select Groups assigned to the application.
For Source attribute, select Group ID from the drop-down menu.
See image.
Click Save.
On the Attributes & Claims page, copy the Claim name for the user.groups [All] and user.givenname attributes.
See image.
In the Azure portal, click Groups.
See image.
Copy the Object Id for the groups you want to map users to in the Deception Admin Portal.
See image.
Log in to the Deception Admin Portal.
Go to Settings > Users & Roles > IdP Providers.
Click the Edit icon for the SAML SSO entry you created for Azure AD.
See image.
In the SAML Provider Details window, under Group-Based SAML Login:
Enable Auto Create User.
For SAML Response Group Attribute, enter the Claim name you copied for the user.groups [All] attribute.
For SAML Response Name Attribute, enter the Claim name you copied for the user.givenname attribute.
Click Add to add a group and map the roles for each group.
For Group Name, enter the Object Id for a group you copied.
Select a role for the group from the drop-down menu.
See image.
Click Save.
